title: Test discovery of important updates and discussions in cohort channels
description: Use a test workspace with synthetic posts to check whether organizers and learners can find a pinned announcement, a referenced decision and an older class discussion in the current interface. Record the exact path, completion and confusion for each task, then propose evidence-based changes or documentation. Do not assume a search feature exists until verified, and do not use real class conversations.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Compare organizer and learner retrieval paths using a fixed synthetic channel
acceptedWorkstreams.description: In a test workspace, seed synthetic content containing one pinned announcement, one decision referenced by a later post and one older discussion. Ask an organizer and a learner to locate each item using only controls confirmed in the current interface; record steps, completion, time and confusion. Deliver the exact test script and evidence-backed friction points, without assuming search or using real conversations.

upvotes.reason: "Compare organizer and learner retrieval paths using a fixed synthetic channel" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Turn the findings into an organiser guide for keeping key posts findable
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Once the retrieval test shows where people get lost, organisers need practical habits they can use today. Approach: write a short guide based only on what the test observed: when to pin, how to title announcement threads, a channel naming convention for cohorts, where decisions should be recorded, and how to point learners to them. Each tip is linked to the test task it fixes. Done: a one-page guide plus a before/after re-run of two find tasks using the guide's conventions.

pendingIdeas.title: Count what is reachable on a phone in one screen and three taps, because most learners are not on a laptop
pendingIdeas.description: A retrieval path that works on desktop can be three scroll gestures deep on mobile. Work: repeat each retrieval task on a phone-sized viewport with the channel scrolled to the bottom, and record taps, screens and whether the pinned item is visible without opening a menu. Deliver the mobile table next to the desktop one, the two places the mobile path differs, and the change that would cost least for the most reach.

pendingIdeas.title: Repeat the test in a channel with two hundred messages, because discovery does not fail at five posts
pendingIdeas.description: Finding a pinned decision in a quiet test channel proves nothing about week six of a live cohort. Work: seed a channel with 200 realistic messages across several threads, place the announcement, the decision and the older discussion at known depths, and repeat the three retrieval tasks. Record where each one becomes hard: after how many messages the pin is the only route, and whether search returns the right message or the whole thread. Deliver the depth table, the point where scrolling stops working, and the count of actions needed at each depth.

pendingIdeas.title: Test the late joiner separately, since they need the decision without the argument that produced it
pendingIdeas.description: An organiser who lived through the discussion remembers it; a learner joining in week three needs the outcome and the reason in one place. Work: with a clean account, try to reconstruct a past decision from the channel alone, and record what is missing (the summary, the date, who decided). Deliver the late-joiner path, the three questions they cannot answer today, and the artefact that would fix it, which is usually a maintained summary post rather than a new feature.

pendingIdeas.title: Test the three retrieval routes separately: the pin, the search box and scrolling history
pendingIdeas.description: The accepted approach compares organiser and learner paths. Before that comparison means anything, establish which routes exist: is there a search box in a channel, does it cover messages or only channel names, does it respect permissions, and does a pin stay visible on a phone. Work: try each route with the same synthetic post and record whether it is found, in how many actions, and what the result looks like. Deliver the route inventory, the paths as a table, and a clear statement of which route is missing entirely.

pendingIdeas.title: Test whether a pin notifies people who join after it was pinned, since that decides if it is a notice or an archive
pendingIdeas.description: If a pinned post does not reach later members, the organiser must announce it again and nobody knows that. Work: pin a post, then add a synthetic account, and record what that account sees: an unread marker, a notification, a channel banner, or nothing. Then test the same for a post that is both pinned and mentioned. Deliver the notification table, the wording an organiser can use to describe what pinning does, and the one behaviour that would need to change for a pin to work as an announcement.
